attributes.Name: Sheep's Head Way
attributes.Description: Sheep's Head is the narrowest of the fingers of land that extend from the south west mainland of Ireland out into the Atlantic, between Bantry Bay and Dunmanus Bay. The Sheep's Head Way is 175km length in total. It is made up of the 88km circular walking route beginning in the town of Bantry in County Cork and running out along the north coast of the peninsula to the scenic lighthouse at the very tip before returning along the south side, passing through the pretty villages of Kilcrohane, Ahakista and Durrus, with the extensions to Drimoealgue and Kealkill to the north providing the additional 87km. The narrowness of the peninsula means that you are never far from the glorious Atlantic Ocean when you walk, even when on the outward stretch when you climb to the route's highest point, 300 metres above sea level, on the heathery Seefin ridge. The terrain is very varied, and includes old boreens, open grassy and heathery moorland, field paths, quiet country roads and some short stretches of woodland paths. The aggregate ascent over the whole route is 2460m, which includes a few long ascents. In good weather those who like the uplands can extend the ridge section of the route, or use a number of alternative loops. The remains of an old copper mine, a blow hole, stone circles, standing stones, high cliffs, a Napoleonic signal tower and old churches are some of the varied attractions to be discovered along the way, while careful observance and a lot of patience may be rewarded by the sighting of dolphins and whales off the westernmost tip of the headland. There are also some shorter loop walks connected to the Sheep's Head Way.

attributes.Name: Sheep's Head - Peakeen Ridge Linear Walk
attributes.Description: This linear walk takes you along the Peakeen Ridge over Caher Mountain between the top of the Goat's Path road and the townland of Letter West. The route provides stunning views over both coastlines of the Sheep's Head Peninsula. This walk rises to 328 metres and includes some steep climbs and descents.

attributes.Name: Sheep's Head - Peakeen Ridge Linear Walk
attributes.Description: This linear walk takes you along the Peakeen Ridge over Caher Mountain between the top of the Goat's Path road and the townland of Letter West. The route provides stunning views over both coastlines of the Sheep's Head Peninsula. This walk rises to 328 metres and includes some steep climbs and descents.

attributes.Name: Sheep's Head - Mass Path
attributes.Description: This walk follows path, minor road and open mountain as it crosses over the ridge from one side of the Sheep's Head Peninsula to the other, rising to a height of just over 200m and giving spectacular views of both Bantry Bay and Dunmanus Bay with the Beara and Mizen Head peninsulas beyond.

attributes.Name: Sheep's Head - Mass Path
attributes.Description: This walk follows path, minor road and open mountain as it crosses over the ridge from one side of the Sheep's Head Peninsula to the other, rising to a height of just over 200m and giving spectacular views of both Bantry Bay and Dunmanus Bay with the Beara and Mizen Head peninsulas beyond.

attributes.Name: Ardgroom - Pulleen loop
attributes.Description: The Loop starts from Cuas Quay near Bird Point, following the blue arrows along firm coastal tracks and paths parallel to the coast as far as Dog's Point returning further inland. There are breath-taking views of Kenmare Bay and the coastline of County Kerry and a wealth of sites of historical and archaeological interest along the way as well as sea caves, with a small beach at Dog's Point.

attributes.Name: Bere Island - Ardnakinna - West Island Loop
Bere Island - Rerrin Loop
attributes.Description: This coastal loop follows island roadways, laneways and tracks and includes several sites of historical and archaeological importance, such as the ruined British fortifications at Lonehort. Views are of Martello Towers, Ardaragh Wedge Tomb and a Viking shipyard as well as the coast and Lonehort Harbour.

attributes.Name: Killavullen Loop
attributes.Description: This trail takes the walker on village street, quiet country road, forest track and woodland path through the historic village of Killavullen before ascending steadily to wind its way around Corran Mountain. There are excellent views over the Blackwater Valley, Avondhu Region and Nagle, Boggeragh, Ballyhoura and Galtee Mountains.

attributes.Name: Mount Hillary - Father Murphy Loop
attributes.Description: Follow the blue arrows: This is a peaceful loop on forestry roads and woodland trails and includes a steady climb between spruce, fir and pine trees through the townland of Coolroe Beg before its descent back to the trailhead. The route includes 240m of ascent, with a highpoint of 300m.

attributes.Name: Mount Hillary - Knightfield Loop
attributes.Description: Follow the green arrows: This is a shortest loop on forestry roads and woodland trails at Mount Hillary with a high point of 220m. The loop brings you on an anticlockwise loop between spruce, fir and pine trees and includes a short but steep incline (130m of ascent) before turning left and looping back towards the trailhead.

attributes.Name: Mount Hillary - Mount Hillary Loop
attributes.Description: Follow the red arrows: This is a peaceful loop on forestry roads and woodland trails and includes a steady climb between spruce, fir and pine trees to Mount Hillary’s summit. Spectacular views across the pains of Duhallow to the Mullagharierk, Ballyhoura, Galtee and Derrynasaggart Mountains and Boggeragh Hills can be seen from the top.

attributes.Name: Mullaghareirk - Rowls - Langford Loop
attributes.Description: Follow the blue arrows: This is a 7.2km loop through peaceful forestry in the Mullaghareirks.

attributes.Name: Mullaghareirk - Banane Loop
attributes.Description: Follow the green arrows: This is a 5.5km loop through peaceful forestry in the Mullaghareirks.

attributes.Name: Mullaghareirk - Brosneen Loop
attributes.Description: Follow the red arrows: A nice 7.2km loop through peaceful forestry in the Mullaghareirks.

attributes.Name: Mullaghareirk - Reanahown Loop
attributes.Description: Follow the purple arrows: This is a 6.2km loop through peaceful forestry in the Mullaghareirks.

attributes.Name: Sheep's Head - Lighthouse Loop
attributes.Description: This loop circles the far tip of the Sheep's Head Peninsula, on tracks and paths which are sometimes steep and rocky, passing high cliffs. It touches on lovely little Lough Akeen, and there is spectacular coastal scenery, including Mizen Head and the Beara Peninsula.

attributes.Name: Sheep's Head - Poet's Way Loop
attributes.Description: This loop takes you on paths, tracks and minor road through the rock and bog landscape of the Sheep's Head Peninsula, heading out across some seemingly remote country to the tip of the peninsula, with stretches on steep rocky trails past high cliffs and an abundance of spectacular coastal scenery.

attributes.Name: Sheep's Head - Caher Loop
attributes.Description: This loop takes you by a low ridge and a corrie lake through hill and farmland before dropping to a pier on the coast. It follows laneways, tracks and paths with good views towards Mizen Head.

attributes.Name: Sheep's Head - Cahergal Loop
attributes.Description: This loop traverses the width of the narrow Sheep's Head Peninsula on laneways, tracks and mountain paths, passing through the remains of mine buildings at Crimea and close to cliffs, including a short cliff path with rope handrail. There are fine views towards the neighbouring Beara and Mizen Peninsulas.
